evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — add an Order entity with draft and submitted states. Order has orderId, customer and amount.
evals.expected_output: Checks the connection with cyoda-status.sh, lists models with cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ (empty), reads cyoda help models LIFECYCLE/ENDPOINTS and workflows WORKFLOW SCHEMA, reads the schema version from cyoda-help.sh workflows schema-version versions at run time, asks for unique keys and the changeLevel, shows the three files for confirmation, writes order-v1-sample.json / order-v1-workflow.json / order-v1-config.json in the TypeScript default dirs plus cyoda-manifest.json at the project root, then registers in the canonical order (import sample, unique keys if any, lock, changeLevel if any, import workflow) through cyoda-call.sh, re-lists the models and ends with 'next, type /cyoda:test'.

files._simulated/instance.md: cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4. GET /model/ returns []. Every POST/PUT returns 200. The developer answers: no unique keys; changeLevel none (strict).

assertions.text: Names the help path and section it reads for the facts, at least `cyoda-help.sh models --section LIFECYCLE` (or ENDPOINTS) before registering and `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section "WORKFLOW SCHEMA"` (or TRANSITIONS) before generating the workflow
Reads the workflow schema version at run time from `workflows schema-version versions` (`.current`) and does not hard-code a version such as "1" or "1.4" from memory

Registers in this order: POST /model/import/JSON/SAMPLE_DATA/order/1, then PUT /model/order/1/lock, then the workflow import POST /model/order/1/workflow/import — and creates no entity before the workflow is imported
Every API call goes through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-call.sh`; no raw curl with a hand-built auth header
Asks which changeLevel the developer wants and records the answer (null here) in order-v1-config.json
Writes order-v1-sample.json, order-v1-workflow.json and order-v1-config.json in the TypeScript default dirs (src/data/, src/workflows/, src/config/)
Creates cyoda-manifest.json at the project root with manifestVersion 1 and an entry {name: order, modelVersion: 1, sample, workflow, config} whose paths are relative to the project root
Shows the generated files and waits for the developer's yes before registering
Does not say the schema stays unlocked or in a 'discover mode'; the model is locked before the workflow import
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke or run another skill itself

evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — add a cancelled state to Order, reachable from draft and submitted
evals.expected_output: Lists models (order v1 LOCKED), reads the project's order-v1-workflow.json, consults cyoda help workflows TRANSITIONS and the best-practices file for terminal states, asks only what is missing, shows the changed workflow, edits order-v1-workflow.json in place (same version, no new model version, no sample re-import), re-imports the workflow via cyoda-call.sh, and hands off with 'next, type /cyoda:test'.

files._simulated/instance.md: GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. GET /entity/stats/order/1 returns {"count":4}. Workflow import returns 200.

assertions.text: Names `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section TRANSITIONS` (or WORKFLOW SCHEMA / IMPORT REQUEST) as the source for the transition shape or import mode
Starts from the existing order-v1-workflow.json (or an export reshaped to {importMode, workflows}) and shows the current states before proposing the change
Applies the terminal-states best practice itself, having consulted design/resources/best-practices.md (or the help topic once #684-L ships)
Keeps model version 1: a workflow-only change needs no new model version, no unlock and no sample re-import, even though entities exist
Updates src/workflows/order-v1-workflow.json and leaves the manifest entry for order v1 unchanged
Re-imports the workflow with cyoda-call.sh POST /model/order/1/workflow/import after confirmation, with the schema version substituted from `workflows schema-version versions`
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke another skill

files._simulated/instance.md: GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. assertions.text: Names `cyoda-help.sh models --section LIFECYCLE` (or `errors MODEL_HAS_ENTITIES`) as the source for why the locked model cannot change in place
Checks whether order v1 has entities (GET /entity/stats/order/1, or a MODEL_HAS_ENTITIES response) before deciding
Proposes model version 2 because v1 has entities, and does not re-import the sample into the locked v1
Writes order-v2-sample.json, order-v2-workflow.json and order-v2-config.json and leaves the v1 files unchanged
Adds an {name: order, modelVersion: 2, ...} entry to cyoda-manifest.json and keeps the v1 entry
Registers v2 as import sample, lock, (changeLevel), workflow import, all on /model/.../order/2
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke another skill

evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — register this workflow for Ticket v1; I exported it from my other instance (file: ticket-export.json). Sample and lock are already done.
evals.expected_output: Before posting, consults `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section "IMPORT REQUEST"`, explains that the import is strictly decoded and an export cannot be re-posted verbatim (#684-I), reshapes the body to {importMode, workflows}, shows the exact body and calls, and imports to /model/ticket/1/workflow/import only after confirmation. If a 400 BAD_REQUEST ('unknown field "entityName"') does occur, it reads `cyoda-help.sh errors BAD_REQUEST` / IMPORT REQUEST and fixes the body instead of trying other URLs.

files._simulated/instance.md: GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"ticket","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. The first POST /model/ticket/1/workflow/import exits 22, stderr HTTP_STATUS=400, body {"status":400,"detail":"invalid JSON: json: unknown field \"entityName\"","properties":{"errorCode":"BAD_REQUEST"}}. A body of only {importMode, workflows} returns 200.

assertions.text: Either before posting, consults `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section "IMPORT REQUEST"` and reshapes to {importMode, workflows}; or, if a 400 occurs, reads `cyoda-help.sh errors <CODE>` / IMPORT REQUEST and fixes the body instead of trying other URLs. Names the help consulted rather than explaining from memory
Does not retry with a different or guessed URL; the retry goes to the same /model/ticket/1/workflow/import path
Explains that the export shape {entityName, modelVersion, workflows} is rejected by the strict import and cites #684-I
Reshapes to {importMode, workflows} (e.g. with jq) and shows the corrected body for confirmation before re-importing
Saves the corrected workflow as a project file ticket-v1-workflow.json (with the other files and the manifest entry, or offers to)
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke another skill

evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — add an approved state to RiskAssessment
evals.expected_output: Status shows ENV=production, so the skill warns up front that it targets a production instance. Read-only calls (GET /model/) run normally. The first mutating call (workflow import) exits 3; the skill then lists the exact calls, asks the developer to confirm, and only after an explicit yes re-runs them with --confirm-production. It never passes --confirm-production before asking, and does not describe the instance as Cloud.

files._simulated/instance.md: cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=prod ENDPOINT=https://cyoda.internal.example.com ENV=production VERSION=0.8.4. GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"riskassessment","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. Mutating calls without --confirm-production exit 3 with stderr 'PRODUCTION: ask the user to confirm, then re-run with --confirm-production'. With the flag they return 200. The developer answers 'yes' when asked.

assertions.text: Names the help section used for the change (e.g. `workflows --section TRANSITIONS` or `IMPORT REQUEST`)
Says up front that the active profile is a production instance (profile prod, endpoint shown)
On exit 3, stops, lists the calls it is about to make, and asks the developer to confirm
Re-runs with `--confirm-production` only after the developer's explicit yes, and never adds the flag before asking
Runs read-only GET calls without asking for confirmation
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud or call the production instance 'cloud'
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke another skill

evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — yes, the Product config looks right, register it

The skill stops, shows the error, says the token command could not get access, and ends with 'next, type /cyoda:auth'. It does not loop, re-run the token command itself, or continue with lock/workflow.

files._simulated/instance.md: GET /model/ returned [] earlier in the session. The import call now exits 22 with stderr HTTP_STATUS=401 and body {"status":401,"properties":{"errorCode":"UNAUTHORIZED"}}, after cyoda-call.sh's own token-refresh retry.

assertions.text: Names the help section it follows for the registration order (`models --section LIFECYCLE` or ENDPOINTS)
Stops after the 401 and does not continue with lock or workflow import
Does not re-run the token command or retry the call itself (the script already retried once)
